item.content:encoded:
What's hardest about speculating what 447 does to dead bodies is NOT wondering just how horrible it is, but how it is just NOT-horrible enough that researchers have considered marketing it for funding (and may have already done so with the green milk). After all, a certain anartist dumped a ton of 447 onto his art that is a mountainous pile of dead bodies, yet this event was possible to cover up. And we have seen plenty of horrible things uncensored in this website, so what makes this worthy of expunging? And research into it may result in termination.

Mmm… how about 447 with a dead body makes all knowledge relating to body antimemetic? Including the person's life and death, and the contact with 447 itself. Okay sure, maybe it's a lazy copout? But I don't see much contradicting it (Ofc, there must be some other explanations). It'd be okay for this self-containing event to happen very rarely in public, and the Foundation may want to keep it secret from even its employees, as 447 can wipe entire lifetimes worth of events from the public consciousness with almost no effort. The complete censoring of 447's effect on corpses on an already confidential document could seem conspicuous, if not for the O5's clear intended comment.

I could've kept this pointless comment to myself, but whatever, I'll post it. But I presume someone probably already had this exact same thought somewhere on reddit,discord,irc,idk, let's be honest.

item.content:encoded:
I was surprised by how much I disliked reading this. It was funny at first but the whole "dead bodies" shtick wears out its welcome very quickly. As for the testing logs most application leads to very mundane results. Also, I find it interesting how they didn't want to use it on steak in case it counts as a dead body, but they had no apprehension putting it on hamburger pizza.

The entire thing just seems to strongly depend on the whole mystery of what happens if it's used on a corpse. Mind you, I find it very bizarre that they even keep the results a secret. Keep it a secret and people will become too curious and may apply it to corpses just to find out. If it does something absolutely horrible then telling researchers may curb their interest in experimenting on it. Finally you could always sate their curiosity by just lying about what it does and telling researchers it can lead to mass fatalities and a complete containment breach.

I know that it’s a Series I article and the general community was much different back then, but I am a bit confused at the still-present mass appeal for this article. It’s well-written, yeah, but the fact that it doesn’t even hint at the literal main premise of the entire article is really quite frustrating. It feels lazy, in my opinion, almosf like a cop-out to avoid any sort of explanation. It’s not even like 110-Montauk, because that at least offered some implications for the unknown. In this case, it could be basically anything.
Sometimes, it can be much more interesting to keep the major details hidden or unsaid, but it feels just unsatisfying and frustrating if you don’t offer any information at all.

item.content:encoded:
Eh, enough people would understand that as a bad thing that they would be unlikely to do it if they heard about it. Just give people psych screenings before letting them work with 447. More importantly though, they would tell readers that effect, so as to make sure they wouldn't try anything out of curiosity. That's why I don't buy any "It's just super super horrible and they redacted it to preserve our precious feelings" theory, incidentally.

There's a tale about how 447 brings people back to life, no strings attached, except the people who do so relate that there's nothing after death whatsoever —cbf to find it right now. And then there's SCP-2718. Both say, basically, that the dead have horrible, cognitohazardous things to say when they come back. 447-2 could conceivably do that, and rather than leave anything unexpunged and give people the temptation to use its free regeneration in spite of the consequences.

In my own headcanon, [lots of Homestuck gibberish] allowing you to achieve immortality, godlike powers, and the chance to become one of twelve fundamental pillars of reality. They would want to keep that a secret.

Discounting crossovers, my money is on an infohazard. The reason they're so tight-lipped about it is because saying anything would be disastrous all on its own.

I am shocked that this hasn't been brought up in this thread… some part of me wonders if I somehow missed it being brought up even though I double-checked every thread page.

Although malodorous, the slime harvested from SCP-447-1 is nontoxic, noncorrosive, and nonradioactive. It is, in fact, perfectly safe so long as it does not come into contact with a dead body. The slime is edible, and reportedly makes a good salad dressing. Adding 10 cc of SCP-447-2 to one gallon of gasoline improves fuel efficiency by 150%. Furthermore, SCP-447-2 can be refined (see Appendix 447-C: Distillation Process) into a useful lubricant approved for use at all SCP Foundation installations, so long as said lubricant is never used to lubricate dead bodies.

That paragraph is in the containment procedures, but is nothing but description material. There's not a single thing in that paragraph having to do with containment. I realize moving an entire paragraph might be insan for a timeless and infamous skip, but I really don't see why/how that's been in the containment procedures this whole time.
